transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brought you in today?

Well, doctor... I guess I'm just having trouble settling down. Since I retired, I thought I'd be relaxing more. But I just... I can't seem to slow down. I'm always up, moving from one little job around the house to the next. All day. It's like I still have a crew waiting on me to get things done, you know? Just... always doing something.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot most days?
No... I wouldn't say that. I don't really sit around worrying about things. Just... busy, I guess.
Have you always been this way, or is this a new change for you?

Always, I suppose. It's not a new thing. ...Even back in grade school, my teachers used to say I was bright, but just... scattered. I was always losing my pencils, or calling out answers in class. They'd always have to remind me to actually finish my work before I could go out for recess. So... yeah. Just always been this way.
When things don’t go your way, do you usually feel that other people should make special accommodations for you?
No... no, I don't think so. I just deal with it, I guess. I don't expect anybody to go out of their way for me.
Do you often lose things you need for tasks, like keys, papers, or glasses?

Yeah... I suppose. I spend a lot of time just... hunting for things. My glasses, keys... my tape measure. Or, uh, this little notebook I use for stories. Half the time I swear I just had it in my hand a few minutes before...
Did these attention and restlessness problems begin before age 12?
Yeah... like I mentioned earlier. It was happening back in grade school. So... yes, I suppose it was before I was twelve.
